item.title: FPI, crude oil, global trends to to steer markets in holiday-shortened week
item.description: Stock market movement would depend on trading activity of foreign investors, crude oil prices and global trends in a holiday-shortened week ahead, analysts said. Equity markets would remain closed on Tuesday for "Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev". "The holiday-shortened week will be influenced by global economic releases, FPI flows and movements in crude oil and the rupee. Domestically, the HSBC Flash India PMI for November, scheduled for Monday, November 23, will provide insights into private-sector activity," Ajit Mishra, SVP -- Research, Religare Broking, said. Globally, investors will track the US GDP data, and consumer confidence for cues on economic growth, he added. item.title: InvIT IPO rush gathers pace, 4-5 trusts likely to go public by Mar 2027
item.description: Four to five privately placed Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) are expected to tap the public markets by March 2027 to raise a combined Rs 17,000 crore, as infrastructure developers increasingly turn to this route to mobilise long-term capital and monetise operational assets, investment bankers said. InvITs have already mobilised around Rs 88,000 crore through equity issuances during FY23-FY25, indicating growing investor appetite for infrastructure-backed investment opportunities, according to the Bharat InvITs Association. Among the proposed public offerings, Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust has filed for a potential Rs 6,000-crore IPO as it seeks to convert from a privately placed to a publicly offered InvIT. Investcorp-backed NDR InvIT Trust is also planning to transition into a public InvIT through an issue of up to Rs 750 crore, while KKR and Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan (OTPP)-sponsored Vertis Infrastructure Trust is also exploring an IPO. item.title: Bitcoin nears USD 60,000: What traders should watch, according to WazirX
item.description: Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], November 20: Bitcoin has lost roughly 21% since the October close and is trading below USD 62,000 and faces sustained US spot ETF outflows. November is often associated with strong gains for the cryptocurrency, but this year its price has moved in the opposite direction. From an October close near USD77,474, Bitcoin fell into the 62,000-64,000 range. By November 20, it was around USD 61,445, roughly one-fifth below the October close and more than 50% below its 2025 peak near USD 126,000.

item.title: Industry body GJC alerts BIS over gold adulteration using Rhenium, Iridium
item.description: The All India Gem and Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) on Friday said it alerted the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) about reports of the alleged use of Rhenium- and Iridium-based alloys to increase gold's weight, and urged the industry and consumers to remain vigilant. "While there have been media reports from certain quarters regarding the possible misuse of materials such as Rhenium and Iridium in gold, we want to assure the entire jewellery industry and all gold buyers that there is absolutely no reason to panic. The Bureau of Indian Standards is treating the matter with utmost seriousness," GJC Chairman Rajesh Rokde said in a statement. According to media reports, Rhenium- and Iridium-based alloys were allegedly used to increase gold's weight without a corresponding increase in purity.
